title: Passes and Valleys, Bernina to the Gotthard

bestPeriod.note: The San Bernardino and Gotthard Tremola pass roads are normally open only from late May or June to October; confirm current status before booking.

summary: A week of high passes and warm valleys, from the Bernina and San Bernardino to the Gotthard's cobbled Tremola and the Verzasca and Maggia.
hook: This is Switzerland's grand traverse in miniature: three high passes, a UNESCO railway line running alongside your car, and a landing in Ticino's palm-lined valleys at the end. Drive it in summer, when every pass road named here is actually open, and budget real time for the hairpins rather than trusting the map's straight-line distance.

snapshot.Base(s): St. Moritz/Pontresina (3 nights), then Locarno/Ascona (3 nights), one night in transit
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 780 km driving, three passes over 2,000 m, valley roads with hairpins
snapshot.Getting There: Rental car from Zürich Airport; return the car in Zürich at trip's end
snapshot.Who It Suits: Confident drivers, couples and families who want mountains and lake towns in one loop

itinerary.title: Zürich to St. Moritz over the Julier Pass
itinerary.morning: Collect the rental car at Zürich Airport and drive south on the A3/A13 to Chur (120 km, 1h15), the gateway to Graubünden's valleys.
itinerary.afternoon: From Chur, climb the Julier Pass (Pass dal Güglia, 2,284 m), one of the rare Alpine passes that stays open year-round; expect grades up to 8% and switchbacks above the treeline. Stop at the Julier's Roman-era cairns near the summit before descending to Silvaplana and St. Moritz (85 km from Chur, roughly 1h30 with stops).
itinerary.evening: Settle into Pontresina and walk the lakeside promenade at St. Moritz for the evening light on the Piz Corvatsch face.
itinerary.dayStats: 205 km, approx. 3h driving · Julier Pass summit 2,284 m.

itinerary.title: Bernina Pass and a dip into Tirano
itinerary.morning: Drive the Bernina Pass road (2,328 m), open year-round though occasionally closed briefly after heavy snowfall even in season. The road runs alongside the UNESCO World Heritage Rhaetian Railway line, watch for the red Bernina Express crossing the Lago Bianco causeway. Stop at the Ospizio Bernina and the lake itself.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue down into Val Poschiavo to Poschiavo village, then cross into Italy at Tirano, a Schengen border with no checkpoint, but carry passports and confirm your rental agreement covers Italy before you go. Walk to the Santuario della Madonna di Tirano and have lunch in the piazza.
itinerary.evening: Return over the Bernina to St. Moritz or overnight in Poschiavo itself.
itinerary.dayStats: 90 km round trip, approx. 2h30 driving · Bernina Pass summit 2,328 m.

itinerary.title: Over the Julier again to San Bernardino
itinerary.morning: Retrace the Julier to Tiefencastel and on to Thusis (95 km from St. Moritz, about 1h45), stopping at the Viamala gorge, a 300 m-deep limestone cut the old Chur-Chiavenna trade route had to cross.
itinerary.afternoon: From Thusis, take the historic San Bernardino Pass road (2,065 m) rather than the road tunnel, it closes roughly November to May, so this only works in the window this trip is built for. Grades reach 9-10% through tight hairpins to San Bernardino village.
itinerary.evening: Overnight in San Bernardino or nearby Mesocco, below the ruined Castello di Mesocco.
itinerary.dayStats: 135 km, approx. 2h45 driving · San Bernardino Pass summit 2,065 m.

itinerary.title: Into Ticino: Bellinzona's three castles
itinerary.morning: Descend the Mesolcina valley to Bellinzona (45 km, 50 min) and walk the UNESCO World Heritage trio of 15th-century castles, Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro, connected by a signed footpath through the old town.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Locarno (25 km, 30 min), Switzerland's warmest corner, and walk the Piazza Grande and the lakeside promenade toward Ascona.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in Locarno's old town, arcaded streets a world away from the passes behind you.

itinerary.title: Verzasca Valley
itinerary.morning: Drive up the Val Verzasca to Lavertezzo and the Ponte dei Salti, a Roman-arched stone bridge over turquoise pools that are genuinely swimmable in summer.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Corippo, Switzerland's smallest municipality, a single street of stone-roofed houses declared a heritage site, then to the Verzasca Dam at Vogorno, a 220 m wall known internationally as the GoldenEye bungee-jump site, worth the stop even just to watch.

itinerary.title: Maggia Valley
itinerary.morning: Drive the Val Maggia to Cevio, then into the Val Bavona, one of the Alps' most dramatically vertical side valleys, its stone ronchi hamlets clinging to the cliff base.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk to the Foroglio waterfall, which drops straight into the valley floor beside the hamlet of the same name, then stop for a swim in the Maggia's clear pools near Ponte Brolla on the way back.
itinerary.evening: Return to Locarno or Ascona for a last Ticino dinner.

itinerary.title: The Gotthard Tremola and home to Zürich
itinerary.morning: Drive Locarno to Airolo on the A2 (60 km, 45 min), then climb the Tremola San Gottardo, the cobbled historic road with 24 hairpins built between the 1830s and 1940s, grades to 9%, up to the Passo del San Gottardo (2,106 m). Stop at the Museo Nazionale del San Gottardo and the old hospice.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the north side into Andermatt and the Urseren valley.
itinerary.evening: Drive on to Zürich via the A2 (150 km, approx. 2h) for the flight home, or take one last night in Andermatt if your schedule allows.
itinerary.dayStats: 215 km, approx. 3h30 driving · Gotthard Pass summit 2,106 m, Tremola grades to 9%.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Walther
accommodationStrategy.description: A 1907 hotel in the Engadin's grand-hotel style, a short walk from the Bernina Express station and well placed for both the Julier and Bernina legs. Ask for a valley-facing room over the Roseg side rather than the road.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 8-10 weeks ahead for July and August.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel San Bernardino
accommodationStrategy.description: A mid-century hotel built for the pass road itself, right at the base of the old San Bernardino climb, useful for breaking the long Julier-to-Ticino day into two manageable legs rather than one exhausting one.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Belvedere
accommodationStrategy.description: An Art Nouveau-era hotel on the hill above Locarno's old town, with lake views and easy walking down to Piazza Grande, and a good base for both the Verzasca and Maggia valley days.

logistics.connectivity: Coverage drops in the Bavona and on the Tremola's upper hairpins; download offline maps for Graubünden and Ticino before setting out each morning.
logistics.emergency: 112 for general emergencies; Rega, the Swiss air rescue service, on 1414 for anything in the mountains.
logistics.money: Cards are widely accepted, but small village kiosks, parking meters and mountain huts often want Swiss franc coins.

other.label: The motorway vignette is mandatory
other.text: An annual sticker or e-vignette, CHF 40 (approx. €42) for the calendar year, is required on all Autobahn/Autostrasse sections (green signs) including the A2 and A13 used on this route. Buy it at the border, at fuel stations, or online before crossing in, driving without one risks a CHF 200 fine.

other.label: Fuel up before the side valleys
other.text: Val Bavona and much of the upper Verzasca have no petrol stations; fill the tank in Locarno or Bellinzona before each valley day.

other.label: Pass closures
other.text: The San Bernardino and Gotthard Tremola pass roads close roughly November to May depending on snow; both have year-round tunnel alternatives (San Bernardino road tunnel, Gotthard road and rail tunnels) if weather forces a detour even in season.

other.label: Cross-border rental
other.text: Confirm before pickup that your rental agreement and insurance cover Italy for the Tirano dip, most Swiss agencies allow it, but not all, and one-way returns to a different depot carry a separate fee.

other.label: Parking realities
other.text: Bellinzona's Castelgrande has a small paid car park at the base; the Ponte dei Salti car park in Lavertezzo fills by mid-morning in July and August, a shuttle bus runs from Tenero on the busiest days.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 for general emergencies; Rega, the Swiss air rescue service, on 1414 for anything in the mountains.

proTips: Drive the Tremola westbound in the early morning, the light comes from behind you on the hairpins and the coach traffic hasn't arrived yet.
Reach the Ponte dei Salti before 09:00; by 11:00 in August the car park is full and the pools are three-deep with people.
Watch the Bernina Express cross the Lago Bianco causeway from the roadside layby just past the Ospizio, the classic angle everyone photographs, for free, from the car.
The San Bernardino old pass road carries a fraction of the Gotthard's traffic for nearly the same drama, treat it as the quiet warm-up before the Tremola.
Buy the vignette online before you land rather than at the border kiosk, where queues build fast on summer weekends.
If you want to watch (or make) a bungee jump at the Verzasca Dam, check the operator's board at the dam car park for the day's jump window rather than assuming it runs continuously.

packingNotes: Layers for pass summits that sit 15-20°C colder than the Ticino valleys below, even in August.
Swimwear and a quick-dry towel for the Verzasca and Maggia pools.
Sunglasses, the glare off high-altitude snow patches and white limestone is sharp even in summer.
A phone mount and offline map download for stretches with no signal.
Comfortable walking shoes for the short climbs at Bellinzona's castles and the Val Bavona hamlets.
Cash in Swiss francs, small denominations, for parking meters and mountain kiosks.
A cool bag or small cooler for picnic stops at passes with no services.
whatCouldGoWrong: **A pass closes for snow, rockfall or maintenance even in summer.** The Gotthard and San Bernardino road tunnels run year-round as fallbacks, and the Bernina Express covers the Bernina corridor by rail if the road shuts.
**The Ponte dei Salti car park is full.** Use the Tenero park-and-ride shuttle rather than circling Lavertezzo's narrow lanes.
**A sudden mountain thunderstorm hits on an exposed pass.** Pull into a marked layby and wait it out, Alpine storms are usually short and visibility on hairpins in heavy rain is genuinely dangerous.
**Your rental car isn't cleared for Italy.** Confirm this at booking, not at the Tirano border, if it isn't covered, skip the dip and spend the extra time at Poschiavo's Baroque old town instead.
**You run low on fuel mid-valley.** Val Bavona and the upper Verzasca have none; treat Locarno and Bellinzona as your last-chance fill-ups before each side trip.
